summary.text: Sam Sutton is the Democratic incumbent state senator for District 22, a South Brooklyn seat with a large Sephardic Jewish community. A longtime Sephardic communal leader who ran a family business for more than three decades and served on the CUNY Board of Trustees, he won a May 2025 special election after Simcha Felder left the seat. He faces Republican/Conservative nominee Nachman Caller in the November 2026 general election.

paragraphs.text: Born in New York City in 1949.
Graduated from Yeshiva of Flatbush (1967) and Yeshiva University (1971).
Led his family business for more than three decades before selling it to an international conglomerate.

Served more than 30 years on the board of Sephardic Bikur Holim, a Brooklyn social-services organization, including five years as its president. His Senate biography also lists him as a co-founder of the Sephardic Community Federation, a supporter of the launch of the New York Cancer Center, and a founding board member of the SAFE Foundation.
Co-founder and board chair of Teach NYS, an organization that advocates for government funding for nonpublic schools such as yeshivas and Jewish day schools.
Nominated by Governor George Pataki to the CUNY Board of Trustees, where he served from 2006 to 2012.

Chosen as the Democratic nominee for the 2025 special election to replace Simcha Felder, who left the Senate seat after winning a New York City Council race; won the May 20, 2025 election over Republican/Conservative candidate Nachman Caller and was sworn in on May 27, 2025.
Chairs the Administrative Regulations Review Commission and sits on the Senate's Aging, Disabilities, Education, Health, New York City Education, and Social Services committees.
According to his Senate biography, he and his wife, Nancy, opened their home to 14 foster children.
